tier_reason: README Performance section gives only two first-party numbers (Serde zero-copy 23 ns vs Tachyon JSON 8 ns, 1,000,000 iterations on {"message":"Hello, world!"}); no benchmark code is in the repo (only src/buffer.rs, lib.rs, macros.rs, value.rs) and no CPU or compiler is stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Serde (zero-copy): 23 ns; Tachyon JSON: 8 ns, 1,000,000 iterations encoding {"message":"Hello, world!"} (~2.9x faster, derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: No benchmark code published in the repo (numbers cannot be reproduced); no CPU model or compiler version stated (.cargo/config.toml builds with target-cpu=native, opt-level=3); single trivial fixed-message microbenchmark; README usage encodes with tachyon_object_noescape! and an unsafe encode call, so the Tachyon side may skip string escaping that serde_json always does; Cargo.toml says 'MIT OR Apache-2.0' but the LICENSE file is MIT only; 0 stars, 3 commits, very small/early project; distinct repo from mrcodechef/Tachyon.JSON which is already on the known list

notes: Numbers match the README exactly; the ~2.9x ratio was unmarked in the record and is now labelled as derived. Metadata (MIT, last commit 2025-07-21, stale, not fork) checked via gh and is correct.

tier_reason: The performance page shows a DOM-parse table against libxml2 (xmlParseMemory) and XSD wall-clock numbers. The benchmark code is public (crates/bench/benches/head_to_head.rs, xsts_compliance.rs), but no CPU, rustc version, flags or libxml2 version is stated anywhere (page, README, COMPARISON.md), so it cannot be A. It is first-party, so C.

corrections.license: Proprietary source-available (Supported Source; LICENSE requires a paid or free-tier license certificate to use the code; not OSI)
corrections.claimed_speedup: DOM parse vs libxml2 xmlParseMemory: ~2.1x median across 21 fixtures, faster on every fixture shown (e.g. gazali_maqasid_ar 599 KB 539 vs 144 MB/s = 3.75x; wikipedia_ww2 252 KB 1170 vs 395 MB/s = 2.96x; swiss_prot 95 MB 177 vs 94 MB/s = 1.88x); W3C XSTS 1.0 wall-clock: schema compile 1.74 s vs 3.96 s (~2.3x), instance validate 1.12 s vs 2.85 s (prose calls this 'parity'), total 2.86 s vs 6.81 s (~2.4x end-to-end, libxml2's 3 timed-out cases excluded); HTML5 parse ~1.02x geomean vs libxml2 (parity)
corrections.workload: DOM parsing of 21 checked-in XML fixtures (11 shown on the page, 15 KB-95 MB) into an owned tree under a 'matched contract' harness (cargo bench -p sup-xml-bench --bench head_to_head); plus W3C XSD 1.0 test suite (XSTS 2006-11-06, 14,328 schemaTests, 25,092 instanceTests) conformance and wall-clock (xsts_compliance bench)
corrections.caveats: No CPU model, rustc version, build flags or libxml2 version disclosed. In head_to_head.rs the timed sup-xml path calls parse_bytes_unchecked, which 'skips the upfront UTF-8 validation' (the harness checks UTF-8 outside the timed region), while libxml2's xmlParseMemory validates inside the timing, which contradicts the page's claim that both sides validate UTF-8. Timing is best-of-N with no warmup (default N=2). The repo's own COMPARISON.md Performance table still says sup-xml vs libxml2 (default) is only ~1.0-1.3x median, which conflicts with the docs page's ~2.1x. The XSD totals exclude libxml2's 3 timed-out schemas, and the page contradicts itself: its table gives instance validate as 1.12 s vs 2.85 s (~2.5x), but the prose says 'parity on validate'. Proprietary license (certificate required, and parsing fails without one), so it is reference only. No independent reproduction found.

notes: All headline numbers are on the docs page. The record's fixture range '7.9KB-95MB' was a misread: chinese1 is 7.9 MB and the smallest fixture shown is 15 KB. The XSD claim is clarified: compile ~2.3x, validate parity, end-to-end ~2.4x. The license is not null: LICENSE is a proprietary Supported Source certificate license (gh reports NOASSERTION). The UTF-8-unchecked timed path is worth flagging during enrichment.

tier_reason: README Performance section has Criterion tables against libxml2 from public bench code (benches/comparison_bench.rs, run with cargo bench --features bench-libxml2), with a bench profile of lto=thin and codegen-units=1 in Cargo.toml. It gives no CPU model, rustc version or libxml2 version, so it is first-party C, not A.

corrections.workload: Criterion benchmarks (benches/comparison_bench.rs) against libxml2 through the Rust `libxml` 0.3 bindings. Parsing covers Atom feed 4.9 KB, SVG 6.3 KB, Maven POM 11.5 KB, XHTML 10.2 KB and a runtime-generated ~374 KB 2000-record document. Serialization covers Atom, Maven POM and the large document. XPath covers four expressions on the Atom and Maven POM fixtures.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc version unstated; Cargo.toml [profile.bench] lto="thin", codegen-units=1
corrections.caveats: No CPU model, rustc version or libxml2 version disclosed. Self-reported by the project. libxml2 is driven through the Rust `libxml` crate wrapper, so serialization (libxml_doc.to_string()) and XPath (Context::evaluate) include wrapper and conversion overhead on the libxml2 side. The README labels the 2.7x XPath row 'Attribute predicate (//book[@id])', but comparison_bench.rs actually runs //dependency[scope='test'] on the Maven POM. Parsing is not a win: 4 of 5 documents parse at or below libxml2 speed (only SVG is 12% faster), so the speed claim rests on serialization (1.5-2.4x) and XPath (1.08-2.7x). The 'Large' document is synthetic (make_large_xml).

notes: Every number in claimed_speedup matches the README tables exactly. XPath 'simple path' is only 8% faster (1.51 vs 1.63 us), which the README rounds into '1.1-2.7x'. Metadata checked via gh is correct (MIT, 86 stars, last commit 2026-08-08, active, not a fork). SupXML's head_to_head.rs also benchmarks against xmloxide, but that does not change this record.
